performance.blocks_next_point: Startup is 588–670 ms with the stand-in (615–952 ms live; 795 ms when I measured), not under half a second. Keystroke to paint is 17 ms median and 18–19 ms p95, just over one 60 Hz frame. That is clearly faster than Obsidian but not yet Sublime.

window_turn: I got the lock after about 6 minutes in the queue and spent about 3 minutes in the window, keyboard only. Earlier judges had left it mid-lesson in Intro Statistics. ⌘K then 'font' found Settings (so search matches synonyms), but ↩ left focus on the page body, and the arrow keys did nothing. ⌘, opened Settings properly: ← → and ↑ ↓ switched the face to Iowan Old Style, the size to 19 and the scheme to Dark, all live with no reload. ⌘P opened the plan layer: exam date as a date, moved rows tagged 'moved up' / 'moved down', and a 'Tell the tutor what changed' line. Esc closed it, and ⇧Tab put the caret in the task's answer line, which turned the task's rule to ink. I typed 'b = 5' ↩ (tutor: 'Not quite', no mark line), then Tab to the talk line and 'by the way, do I need to memorise the t table?' (stand-in canned reply, 'nothing here is marked', the task stayed pinned and grey at the foot). Then 'back to the task' (the task re-activated with the caret back in it) and the right answer (tutor 'Right:', again no mark line, since retries aren't first tries). ⌘Y showed the record in words ('standard error of a mean — Thu 12 Nov, not right yet'), and ⌘/ showed 1/2/3 help with ⌥1–3 for confidence. Measured typing: median 17 ms, p95 19 ms, max 20 ms, startup reported 795 ms. Apart from opening Settings from ⌘K, I never needed the mouse. I put the settings back to Charter / 17 / Like the Mac and released the lock.
